featureRef: 6.13 Competency / standards-based grading — subject skills only
name: Rate a student against the academic skills a subject teaches, beside the overall percentage
priorityReason: Valuable, but the school can report a percentage and a grade without it.

goal.capability: to define the skills a subject teaches and rate each student against them
goal.outcome: a result shows where a student is strong and weak inside a subject, not only what they scored overall

secondaryActors.involvement: Rates each of their own students against the skills of the subject they teach.
Sees the skill breakdown beside the overall result.

additional.description: A subject's marks are submitted, which puts the skill ratings alongside them.

preconditions.condition: The class and subject exist, since skills are defined per class and per subject.
An authenticated session exists. Defining requires the Coordinator; rating requires the subject teacher.
A skill list and a rubric exist for the class and subject before any rating can be given (BR-2).
The subject's marks exist, since the ratings are stored alongside them.

postConditions: A skill list exists for the class and subject, with a rubric of achievement bands attached to each skill.
Every student in the class carries a rating against each skill of that subject, given by the teacher who teaches it.
The ratings are stored alongside that subject's marks, so the two are read together rather than separately.
The student's result shows the overall percentage and grade with the subject-skill ratings reported beside them.
Only academic subject skills were rated. Classroom conduct and co-curricular activity were not, since neither belongs here.
A teacher rated only the students of the subject they teach, and no others.
A skill added or changed after ratings were given did not silently alter what a teacher had already recorded.

dataFields.name: Class
dataFields.validation: Skills are defined per class as well as per subject (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Skill
dataFields.validation: An academic skill the subject teaches. 2 to 100 characters (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Skill description
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. What the skill covers.
dataFields.example: Solving linear and quadratic equations, and manipulating algebraic expressions.

dataFields.name: Rubric band
dataFields.validation: An achievement band on the rubric attached to the skill. Every skill carries a rubric (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Band description
dataFields.validation: What the band means, so a rating is interpretable by a parent (BR-3).
dataFields.example: Solves two-step problems independently and checks the answer.

dataFields.name: Band order
dataFields.validation: Where the band sits, from lowest to highest.

dataFields.name: Rating
dataFields.validation: The band the teacher rates the student at, per skill (BR-4).
dataFields.lookupSource: Bands of the rubric attached to that skill

dataFields.name: Note
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters per student. What the rating alone does not explain.
dataFields.example: Strong on manipulation, hesitant with word problems.

dataFields.name: Rated by
dataFields.validation: The subject teacher who gave the rating (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Retire reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters. Required when retiring a skill (BR-9).
dataFields.example: Merged into Problem solving from this session.

businessRules.rule: Skills are defined per class and per subject. Algebra and geometry within Mathematics are skills of that subject in that class, not of the school.
Every skill carries a rubric of achievement bands. A rating with no rubric behind it is a number nobody can interpret.
Each band states what it means. A parent reading Developing must be able to see what the school means by it.
The subject teacher rates each student against each skill of their own subject. A teacher does not rate a subject they do not teach.
The ratings are stored alongside that subject's marks, so the two are read together. A skill profile held apart from the mark is a second record nobody opens.
The student's result shows the overall percentage and grade with the subject-skill ratings reported beside them, not instead of them.
This use case covers academic subject skills only. Classroom conduct — participation, effort, attentiveness, punctuality — is assessed by the class teacher across all subjects and is not rated here.
Co-curricular activity — sports, societies, competitions, school representation, positions of responsibility — is a record of what happened rather than a rating, and is not held here either.
A skill is retired rather than deleted, with a reason, and the ratings already given against it stay readable.
Changing a rubric band's meaning does not change a rating already given. The rubric in force when the rating was made is recorded with it.
A rating is optional per student where the teacher has no basis for one, and an unrated skill reads as unrated rather than as the lowest band.
The ratings are released with the result, and not before. A skill profile visible before the school has agreed the result is a result released early by another name.

transitions.condition: Retired with a reason. Ratings already given stay readable (BR-9).
A band is chosen for the student and skill.
The subject's result is released and the ratings go with it (BR-12).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Examination → Subject skills → Define skill
basicFlow.userAction: Defines the academic skills the subject teaches for that class.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Stores each skill against the class and subject.

basicFlow.userAction: Attaches a rubric of achievement bands to each skill, each band stating what it means.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires every skill to carry a rubric and every band to carry its meaning.

basicFlow.userAction: Rates each student in the class against each skill of their own subject.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Offers only the bands of the rubric attached to that skill, and only the teacher's own subject.
Stores the ratings alongside that subject's marks, with the rubric in force recorded against each.
Puts the ratings beside the overall percentage and grade on the student's result.
Releases the ratings with the result and not before.

basicFlow.userAction: Reads the skill breakdown beside the overall result.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows each skill, its rating and what the band means.

alternateFlows.condition: The teacher has no basis for rating a skill
alternateFlows.behaviour: The skill is left unrated and reads as unrated rather than as the lowest band. A rating invented to fill a gap is worse than none (BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: A skill is no longer taught
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is retired with a reason and the ratings already given against it stay readable (BR-9).
Ratings already given keep the rubric in force when they were made, so a past rating stays interpretable (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A teacher teaches two subjects in the class
alternateFlows.behaviour: They rate against the skills of each subject separately, and against no subject they do not teach (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The subject's result has not been released
alternateFlows.behaviour: The ratings are not visible to the student or the guardian either, since a skill profile released early is a result released early (BR-12).

exceptions.condition: A band is saved with no description

exceptions.condition: A teacher rates a subject they do not teach
exceptions.messageShown: You do not teach this subject.

exceptions.condition: A rating is chosen that is not a band of that skill's rubric
exceptions.messageShown: Choose a band from the rubric attached to this skill.

exceptions.condition: A skill is defined that describes classroom conduct rather than an academic skill
exceptions.systemResponse: It is accepted, but conduct belongs elsewhere and is not rated here (BR-7).
exceptions.messageShown: Participation and effort are assessed by the class teacher across all subjects, not here.

exceptions.condition: A skill is defined that describes a co-curricular activity
exceptions.systemResponse: Co-curricular activity is a record of what happened, not a rating, and is not held here (BR-8).
exceptions.messageShown: Sports and societies are recorded elsewhere, not rated here.
A skill is retired, not deleted. Ratings already given must stay readable.

exceptions.condition: A guardian opens the breakdown before the result is released
exceptions.messageShown: Results for this exam have not been released.

outOfScope.item: Classroom conduct — participation, effort, attentiveness and punctuality — assessed by the class teacher across all subjects
Co-curricular activity — sports, societies, competitions and positions of responsibility — which is a record rather than a rating
Calculating the overall percentage and grade
Producing the report card the breakdown appears on

departures.requirement: Only academic subject skills are rated here. Conduct and co-curricular activity have their own records, and nothing in this use case creates a second place to hold them.
The rubric in force when a rating was made is stored with it, so a past rating stays interpretable after the wording changes.
An unrated skill is reported as unrated everywhere, and is never treated as the lowest band in any calculation or display.
Ratings are not visible before the subject's result is released.
Skills, rubrics and ratings are retained 7 years, matching the results they sit beside.

openQuestions.question: Who defines the skill list in practice — the Coordinator alone, or with the subject teachers?
openQuestions.assumption: The Coordinator as modelled. Teachers know the subject better.

openQuestions.question: Are the rubric bands the same across every skill and subject, or set per skill?
openQuestions.assumption: Per skill as modelled. One school-wide rubric would be simpler.

openQuestions.question: Is a student rated once per exam, or once per term regardless of exams?
openQuestions.assumption: Per exam as modelled. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Should a skill rating carry any weight in the overall result, or sit purely beside it?
Where does classroom conduct actually get assessed, given it is explicitly out of scope here?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified anywhere in the module.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
